Lung cancer screening: am I eligible?

A yearly low-dose CT scan can find lung cancer early, when it is much more treatable. Only about 1 in 5 people who qualify get screened.

Who should be screened

  • Age 50 to 80Adults in this age range with a heavy smoking history.
  • 20 pack-years or moreSee below for how to count pack-years.
  • You smoke now, or you quitThe U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (2021) includes people who quit within the past 15 years. The American Cancer Society (2023) includes former smokers no matter how long ago they quit.

How to count pack-years

Multiply the packs you smoked per day by the number of years you smoked. One pack a day for 20 years is 20 pack-years. Half a pack a day for 40 years is also 20 pack-years. If your smoking changed over time, add up each period.

What the test is like

  • It is a CT scan of the chest with a low dose of radiation. It takes a few minutes. No needles and no dye.
  • It is repeated once a year while you still qualify.
  • Many scans show small spots (nodules). Most are not cancer. Your doctor may recommend a repeat scan to watch them.

Questions to ask your doctor

  1. Based on my smoking history, do I qualify for screening?
  2. Where will my scan be done, and who will explain the results?
  3. What happens if a spot is found?
  4. What help can I get to quit smoking?

Want to quit? Free, confidential help: 1-800-QUIT-NOW (1-800-784-8669) · En español: 1-855-DÉJELO-YA (1-855-335-3569)
